xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4838: Phone app (iOS): push registration and Notification Service Extension decryption

plan.title: Phone app (iOS): push registration and Notification Service Extension decryption
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: One platform capability (iOS notifications) whose Swift package, NSE target, shared Keychain, JS registration and tap routing must ship together for epic AC-11; the epic already split Android (PAN-4840), Live Activity (PAN-4839), release (PAN-4841) and docs (PAN-4842) into siblings. The file count is inflated by Xcode artifacts (two entitlements, two Info.plists, pbxproj) and Capacitor-regenerated files (CapApp-SPM/Package.swift, capacitor.settings.gradle, bun.lock).

narratives.Problem: The machine already seals needs-you notifications to each phone's push key and the directory forwards them to APNs with placeholder text, but the iOS app neither registers its APNs token with the directory nor decrypts the payload, so an iPhone shows nothing (no registration) or only 'Overdeck · Something needs you'.
narratives.Proposal: Add a local Swift package (OverdeckPush, swift-sodium 0.9.1) holding crypto_box_seal_open, the content rewrite and the Keychain store; move the push key pair into the shared Keychain group $(AppIdentifierPrefix)ai.overdeck.shared; add a Notification Service Extension target that opens s and rewrites title, body and userInfo, falling back to the placeholder; add @capacitor/push-notifications with AppDelegate forwarding; register the token from apps/mobile/src/native/push.ts (iOS only) on token change and each directory online transition with apsEnvironment from a native #if DEBUG method; route taps to the payload's machine and a validated /m path; add a Notifications switch in Settings; verify on the Mac rig with a sodium-native fixture, swift test and simctl push, and run the real-APNs check when /healthz reports apns:true (else hand epic AC-11 to PAN-4841).
narratives.NonGoals:
- Android registration or the FCM service (PAN-4840); pushSupported() stays iOS-only
- The Live Activity, its push token, or App Groups (PAN-4839)
- Apple App ID, APNs key, directory secrets, signing team in the project, TestFlight (PAN-4841)
- User docs beyond one paragraph in configuration/push-notifications.mdx (PAN-4842)
- Any change to services/connect, packages/contracts or src/lib/push/native-provider.ts
- Calling PUT /api/phones/self/push-key, or migrating existing Keychain items
- Calling PushNotifications.unregister()
- Lock-screen actions (reply, approve), badges or custom sounds

autoDecisions.summary: libsodium for the NSE comes from swift-sodium 0.9.1 inside a new local Swift package apps/mobile/ios/OverdeckPush that both targets link.
autoDecisions.rationale: The epic names swift-sodium; a local package mirrors the existing CapApp-SPM reference, keeps pbxproj edits small, and makes the decrypt testable with swift test on the rig.

autoDecisions.summary: The shared Keychain group is $(AppIdentifierPrefix)ai.overdeck.shared (no App Group in this issue).
autoDecisions.rationale: The epic W-IOS1 and PAN-4837 C-5 name this group; only the push key needs sharing, and an App Group has no consumer until PAN-4839.

autoDecisions.summary: No Keychain migration and no PUT /api/phones/self/push-key call.
autoDecisions.rationale: No iOS install exists yet (ACCEPTANCE.md: iOS not testable), and the push key changes only on reset(), which also unpairs every machine.

autoDecisions.summary: apsEnvironment comes from a native OverdeckKeys.pushEnvironment() using #if DEBUG.
autoDecisions.rationale: The web bundle is identical across Xcode configurations; the epic says sandbox for Debug and production for Release, and the directory defaults a missing value to production.

autoDecisions.summary: Registration is iOS-only via pushSupported(); PAN-4840 widens it.
autoDecisions.rationale: @capacitor/push-notifications register() throws on Android without Firebase, which is PAN-4840's scope.

autoDecisions.summary: The Settings notifications switch ships here.
autoDecisions.rationale: Epic W-APP1 lists it and PAN-4837 C-8 deferred it to PAN-4838/4839/4840; epic hazard H-4 needs a place to explain denied permission.

autoDecisions.summary: Epic AC-11's real-iPhone run happens here only if healthz reports apns:true; otherwise rig evidence is recorded and AC-11 is handed to PAN-4841's TestFlight run with a comment and a flywheel tell.
autoDecisions.rationale: healthz reported apns:false on 2026-11-03, the APNs secrets are an operator action in PAN-4841, and no pipeline role can drive a physical iPhone.

items.title: Sealed-push fixture and Simulator payload tool (WI-1)

narrative.Action: PRD .pan/drafts/PAN-4838.md WI-1. Write tests/fixtures/phone-push/generate.mjs (sodium-native via createRequire; phone pair from crypto_box_seed_keypair seed Buffer.alloc(32,0x2a), wrong pair seed 0x17; cases 'question' and 'unicode' exactly as listed in the PRD; wrongKey = question payload sealed to the wrong pair) and commit its output sealed-push.json. Write seal-apns.mjs exporting apnsFixture({publicKeyHex,title,body,machine,url,kind,tag}) with a CLI guard, producing the 'Simulator Target Bundle' + placeholder aps block + s. Write tests/unit/lib/push/phone-push-fixture.test.ts that opens every case with openSealed from src/lib/anywhere/sealed-box.ts.

items.title: Given the committed sealed-push.json, when the test opens each case with openSealed and the fixture key pair, then it returns the case payload byte-for-byte as JSON, including the non-ASCII title.
Given wrongKey.sealed, when openSealed runs with the fixture key pair, then it returns null.

Given apnsFixture({ publicKeyHex: fixture key, title, body }), when the test opens its s, then the payload title equals the given title and aps.alert equals { title: 'Overdeck', body: 'Something needs you' } with mutable-content 1.
OverdeckPush Swift package: open, rewrite, Keychain (WI-2)

verify_commands: rig (ssh -i ~/.ssh/gauntlet_air eltmon@<rig-ip>, apps/mobile/README.md 'Run in the iOS Simulator'): rsync apps/mobile/ios/OverdeckPush and tests/fixtures/phone-push, then cd ~/overdeck-mobile/apps/mobile/ios/OverdeckPush && swift test
expected_outputs: swift test exits 0 and runs SealedPushTests and PushContentTests
metadata.parallelSafeReason: swift test runs in its own package subtree on the rig and touches no other item's files; it is edge-ordered before every item that builds the Xcode project.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-2. Create apps/mobile/ios/OverdeckPush/ (Package.swift with swift-sodium exact 0.9.1, platforms iOS 15 / macOS 12) with Sources/OverdeckPush/{SealedPush,PushContent,KeychainStore,PushKeys,Hex}.swift and Tests/OverdeckPushTests/{SealedPushTests,PushContentTests}.swift, using the exact signatures in the PRD. KeychainStore is the App target's file made public with an optional group parameter and removeAll(sharedGroup:). Tests read tests/fixtures/phone-push/sealed-push.json via #filePath (seven deletingLastPathComponent() calls reach the repo root). Checkpoint CP-1: if swift-sodium 0.9.1 does not build, pin its newest default-branch revision; if that fails, pan tell flywheel-orchestrator and stop.

items.title: Given the sodium-native fixture, when SealedPush.open runs with the fixture key pair, then it returns each case's PhonePushPayload, and returns nil for wrongKey, for one flipped base64 character, for 'not base64' and for a 31-byte key.

Given a CryptoKit Curve25519.KeyAgreement.PrivateKey and a v1 payload sealed with Sodium().box.seal to its raw public key, when SealedPush.open runs with the raw key pair, then it returns the payload.

Given a UNMutableNotificationContent holding the alert text 'Overdeck' / 'Something needs you' and userInfo with s, when PushContent.apply runs, then title, body and threadIdentifier equal the payload's title, body and tag, userInfo has url, machine, kind and tag, and s is removed.
Given a payload with an empty title, when PushContent.apply runs, then the content keeps the title 'Overdeck'.

Add the pushEnvironment plugin method to OverdeckKeysPlugin.swift (#if DEBUG sandbox, else production), add pushEnvironment(): Promise<{ apsEnvironment: ApsEnvironment }> to the OverdeckKeysPlugin interface in apps/mobile/src/native/keys.ts, return { apsEnvironment: 'sandbox' } from OverdeckKeysWeb, and test it in keys.test.ts. Push registration in the shell sends push-register to the directory (WI-7)

expected_outputs: push.test.ts passes with one test per rule R1-R8

narrative.Action: PRD WI-7. Create apps/mobile/src/native/push.ts with pushSupported (iOS only), notificationsEnabled, startPush and the PushController interface, implementing rules R1-R8 exactly; tests in apps/mobile/src/native/__tests__/push.test.ts, one it block per rule. In ShellApp.tsx add push to Services, start it next to createDirectory only when pushSupported(), stop it in the cleanup. Never call PushNotifications.unregister(); never log the token. R4 starts from directory.state at startPush time; if already online it acts once at start.

items.title: Given a stored token and notifications on, when the fake directory changes from connecting to online, then startPush sends exactly one { type: 'push-register', platform: 'ios', token, apsEnvironment: 'sandbox' } frame, and a later machine-list notification with the state still online sends nothing.
Given iOS reports permission 'prompt', when startPush starts, then it calls requestPermissions and, on 'granted', register; on 'denied' it never calls register and permission reads 'denied'.
Given a registration event whose value fails /^[0-9A-Za-z:_.-]{1,4096}$/, when it arrives, then nothing is sent and localStorage overdeck.pushToken keeps its old value.
Given notifications turned off with disable(), when the directory is online or next becomes online, then startPush sends { type: 'push-unregister' } and no push-register.
Given platform 'android' or 'web', when pushSupported runs, then it returns false, and ShellApp never calls startPush.
Tapping a notification opens the machine and screen (WI-8)

narrative.Action: PRD WI-8. Create apps/mobile/src/shell/notificationTap.ts with safeMobilePath, tapTarget and installNotificationTap (sessionStorage overdeck.notificationHandled dedupe by notification id; ignore when signed out), tests in apps/mobile/src/shell/__tests__/notificationTap.test.ts, and in ShellApp.tsx install it in an effect after boot is ready when pushSupported(); open sets the current machine then navigates, or goes to '/' for an unknown machine. Checkpoint CP-3 (cold launch) is checked in WI-10.

items.title: Given the URLs https://evil.example/m, //evil.example/m, javascript:alert(1), /settings, /mx, '', undefined and 42, when safeMobilePath runs, then each returns '/m', and '/m?subject=a' and '/m/x?y=1' are returned unchanged.

Given notification data { machine: <paired environmentId>, url: '/m?subject=a' }, when tapTarget runs, then it returns { kind: 'machine', environmentId, path: '/m?subject=a' }; an unknown machine returns { kind: 'machines' }; data without machine returns null.
Given two pushNotificationActionPerformed deliveries with the same notification id, when installNotificationTap handles them, then open is called once, and it is not called at all while signed out.
Notifications switch in Settings (WI-9)

narrative.Action: PRD WI-9. Add the optional notifications prop to SettingsScreen.tsx with the role=switch button and the two hint texts exactly as written in the PRD, add usePushState(controller) to push.ts, pass notifications from ShellApp.tsx only when services.push is set (onChange calls enable or disable), and add apps/mobile/src/shell/__tests__/SettingsScreen.test.tsx.

items.title: Given SettingsScreen without the notifications prop, when it renders, then no element with role switch is present.
Given notifications { enabled: true, permission: 'granted' }, when the switch renders and is clicked, then it has aria-checked='true' and onChange is called with false.
Given permission 'denied', when SettingsScreen renders, then it shows the text 'Notifications are off for Overdeck in iOS Settings.'

metadata.acJustification: Four ACs map to the four evidence lines epic AC-11 needs; the last one is conditional on PAN-4841's APNs secrets (D-16).
metadata.readinessReason: All Mac-rig verification shares one ~/overdeck-mobile checkout, one DerivedData and the rig's Simulators, so items that build on the rig must never run in parallel with each other.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-10. On the rig with a team-signed Simulator build: read the push public key from the log, seal with tests/fixtures/phone-push/seal-apns.mjs, terminate the app, simctl push the real and the wrong-key payloads, screenshot both, check the cold-launch tap (CP-3), and record CP-4 if simctl does not run the NSE. Then check https://connect.overdeck.ai/healthz: with apns:true and a device, run the real AskUserQuestion push (title within 10 s, tap opens the card, wrangler tail shows no title); with apns:false or no device, record the healthz output, comment on PAN-4841 that its first TestFlight install must run epic AC-11, and pan tell flywheel-orchestrator. Write everything to the new ACCEPTANCE.md section; delete the Simulator.

items.title: Given the app terminated on the rig Simulator, when simctl push delivers a payload sealed to its push key, then ACCEPTANCE.md records a screenshot showing the payload's real title, or the CP-4 finding with the Xcode version when the extension did not run.
Given a payload sealed to the wrong key, when simctl push delivers it, then the recorded screenshot shows 'Overdeck' and 'Something needs you'.
Given a notification tapped while the app is terminated, when the app opens, then ACCEPTANCE.md records whether it opened the payload's machine at its /m path and which CP-3 path was used.

Given healthz reports apns:true and a device is available, when a desktop AskUserQuestion fires, then ACCEPTANCE.md records the real title shown within 10 s and no title text in wrangler tail; otherwise it records the healthz output and links the PAN-4841 comment that carries epic AC-11.
Document iOS notifications in the README, the push page and the codebase map (WI-11)

narrative.Action: PRD WI-11. Update apps/mobile/README.md (layout rows for ios/OverdeckPush and ios/App/NotificationService, rig rsync of OverdeckPush and tests/fixtures/phone-push, the team-signed build, swift test, the seal-apns + simctl push recipe, the Keys section for the shared group and D-5 fallback and pushEnvironment, a new 'Notifications (iOS)' section, and the 'What it cannot do yet' list), add the placeholder paragraph to configuration/push-notifications.mdx 'The Overdeck app', and update the apps/mobile row of .overdeck/context/codebase/architecture.md.

items.title: Given apps/mobile/README.md, when a reader opens it, then it has a 'Notifications (iOS)' section describing registration, the Settings switch, the fixed 'Overdeck · Something needs you' text on failure and tap routing, and its Keys section names the $(AppIdentifierPrefix)ai.overdeck.shared group the extension reads.

Given configuration/push-notifications.mdx, when a reader opens 'The Overdeck app', then it says the iPhone decrypts on the phone and otherwise shows 'Overdeck · Something needs you', and that the switch is in the app's Settings.

Given .overdeck/context/codebase/architecture.md, when a reader opens the apps/mobile/ row, then it names the NotificationService extension and the OverdeckPush Swift package, and the file ends with exactly one last-verified line.
